posts.author: Silvemaar
posts.body:
Hello! I've heard you accept middle aged men in your cool game-development club, so here I am.
In all seriousness, I'm not completely new. I've dabbed into RPG Maker 2003 before, but that was more to check out possibilities of such engines.
These days I own MZ and I actually use it in my spare time for a serious project. It is an old school JRPG (shocking, I know). It is also a one man project that relies mostly on vanilla resources, as I am no artist. Hopefully, it will evolve into a decent, fun game that also shows off my writing and ideas a bit.
I've been going through your posts on the forums in past weeks and there are some really great resources and tips & tricks available (some of which were a big help) - so big
THANK YOU
for that!

posts.author: ZombieKidzRule
posts.body:
Welcome! Glad you said hello! This is a pretty great place to get information, ask questions, find resources, learn new stuff, and just generally socialize with like minded people.
Good luck on your projects and remember to enjoy what you do!
@Erif
Old school depends on how old you are. For instance, for me, old school is the original CRPG games from the 80s and maybe early 90s.
When I hear a game from the early 2000s referred to as old school, it makes me shudder.
